title: Board Policy on Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) Across a Member's Service Accounts
content:
# Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) Across a Member's Service Accounts

## Policy

1. A member may have Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) on several service accounts, and each plan levels one account's charges only.
2. A service account carries at most one plan in enrolled, active, exit pending or removed-for-nonpayment status at a time.
3. No maximum is set on the number of plans one member may hold across the member's service accounts.

## Application

- Clause 1 counts plans account by account. A member with a home meter, a shop meter and a well meter may have a plan on each of them, and each plan levels only the charges of its own account. One plan never levels the charges of two accounts.
- Clause 2 is checked against the cooperative's system records for the service account itself. A plan on another account of the same member has no bearing on it.
- A plan in ended status is not one of the four statuses in clause 2, so a service account whose only plan has ended carries no open plan under this policy.

## Status reference for clause 2

| Status of an existing plan on the same service account | Counts as the account's one plan under clause 2 |
|---|---|
| enrolled | Yes |
| active | Yes |
| exit pending | Yes |
| removed for nonpayment | Yes |
| ended | No |

## Hypothetical cases

- *Hypothetical:* a member holds Farm Budget Billing in active status on a Schedule FH Farm and Home Service account and asks about a plan on a second Schedule R Residential Service account that has no plan. This policy places no limit on the second account, because the active plan is on another account.
- *Hypothetical:* a service account has a plan in exit pending status. Under clause 2 that account already carries its one plan, so a second plan on it would exceed the limit while the first remains exit pending.
- *Hypothetical:* a service account has a plan that was removed for nonpayment and is still in that status. It counts as the account's one plan until it moves to ended.
